subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Durable ADV evidence for the last 10 days shows a healthy prep/gate pipeline (100% TDD compliance flag, 0.857 gate completion rate is the standard 6/7 pre-release measure, low retry density) but three concrete, source-backed instrumentation/context gaps. (1) The single most frequent AGENT problem is not a task failure but an EVIDENCE-INTEGRITY gap: adv-engineer sub-agent reports consistently claim verification commands (pnpm run typecheck, pnpm run schemas:check, grep, vitest) that carry no adv_run_test evidence, surfaced as consumer_warnings kind=verification_missing on essentially every sampled engineer report. Verification is asserted in prose, not durably captured, so acceptance leans on self-reported strings. (2) adv-researcher research packs ARE used at the design gate (validator + leverage scout), but their typed reports are frequently 'persistence degraded' due to workflow reachability, so research coverage is real while its durable trace is lossy. (3) Follow-up capture is over-productive relative to drain: 286 agenda items, dominated by pending subagent-followup, versus 13 wisdom entries with wisdom_reuse_hits=0 in all 19 reflections — the system captures learnings but does not measurably reuse them. Phase friction, by per_gate elapsed, concentrates in planning (human HITL approval latency) and acceptance (review + full-suite verification), not execution. MOST-USED artifacts: proposal, agreement, design, contract (present in every sampled change). LEAST-USED / least-durable: executiveSummary (only on archived changes), problem-statement (problemStatementExists=false widely; folded into proposal), and durable per-command verification evidence. Prep-to-implementation alignment is structurally strong (contract_refs implements/verifies/respects on tasks; briefing packets consumed) but the engineer's ACTUAL verification is under-instrumented. Separating observed fact from missing instrumentation: retry/friction counts are LOW but that is partly because friction is only recorded when a retry or blocker fires — silent verification_missing warnings are NOT counted as friction, so reflection friction metrics understate the real evidence gap.

validation.notes: Read-only audit answered all six research questions with source-backed counts and explicit denominators. Confidence medium: findings rest on durable ADV state (change/reflection/wisdom/agenda/subagent-report reads), which is authoritative for what it records, but adv-researcher/adv-engineer context-adequacy and research-pack-use questions are partly limited by missing instrumentation (degraded report persistence, no reuse counter, no per-command verification ledger for shell-run commands). No architecture blocker; recommendations are measurable follow-ups, not fixes required for this read-only change.

tradeoffs: Reflection friction metrics are cheap and durable but under-count silent evidence gaps (verification_missing warnings are not friction_items), so 'low friction' overstates health.
Follow-up capture (286 agenda items) maximizes recall of drive-by findings at the cost of an unbounded pending backlog and near-zero measured reuse of promoted wisdom.
Delegating apply work to adv-engineer preserves main-context hygiene but shifts verification to self-reported command strings unless adv_run_test is mandated, weakening durable proof.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat low retry_density / 0.857 gate rate as evidence the pipeline has no problems
alternatives_considered.rationale: Those metrics only measure recorded retries/gates; the dominant real issue (verification_missing) is invisible to them. Absence of recorded friction is not absence of friction.

alternatives_considered.option: Recommend a large workflow redesign of the acceptance gate
alternatives_considered.rationale: Simplicity bias: the evidence points to targeted instrumentation gaps (mandate adv_run_test for engineer verification; persist researcher reports reliably; add wisdom-reuse counter), not a gate-shape defect. Prefer boring, measurable fixes.

alternatives_considered.option: Enforce adv_run_test for all engineer-reported verification commands and count verification_missing as first-class friction
alternatives_considered.rationale: Closes the largest observed gap structurally (P33: structural over heuristic) and makes acceptance evidence machine-backed rather than prose-asserted, with minimal surface change.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Land measurable follow-ups (as separate approved changes): (a) make adv-engineer verification route through adv_run_test so consumer_warnings kind=verification_missing drops to ~0, and surface that warning count as a first-class reflection friction metric; (b) fix adv-researcher/design-validator report persistence so 'persistence degraded' design gates become the exception, and add a counter of research-pack reports persisted vs degraded; (c) add a wisdom_reuse instrumentation path so wisdom_reuse_hits stops being uniformly 0; (d) add an agenda drain/triage SLO metric given the 286-item pending subagent-followup backlog.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Report findings to orchestrator as-is (read-only audit). Prioritized measurable follow-ups: 1) Mandate adv_run_test for adv-engineer verification and elevate verification_missing to a counted friction category (highest leverage — it is the single most frequent observed agent-evidence problem, present on ~every sampled engineer report). 2) Make adv-researcher/validator report persistence reliable and count persisted-vs-degraded research packs. 3) Instrument wisdom reuse (currently 0/19). 4) Add an agenda-drain metric (286 pending-heavy items). Denominators, confidence, and limitations are in the findings body; treat missing instrumentation as unknown, not negative.
follow_ups: Packet anchors TASK_SCOPE/IN_SCOPE/OUT_OF_SCOPE/DONE_WHEN/STOP_WHEN/VERIFICATION were not provided verbatim in briefing-packet form; proceeded with the prompt scope per policy.

No adv-engineer briefing-packet sample was inspected directly (adv_change_show include.briefingPacket not run); adv-engineer context-adequacy is inferred from persisted engineer reports (context_update_for_adv, scope_drift=null, blockers=[]) rather than from a rendered packet — a follow-up could render one packet to confirm.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: This is a read-only, self-referential evidence audit of ADV's own workflow. The design is well-constructed for its scope. Contract coverage is complete: all AC1-AC6, SC1-SC3, C1-C3, DONT1-3 have an explicit mapping in the design's Contract Coverage section and are traceable to procedure steps and key decisions. The evidence-class model (observed presence / contract-required consumption / uninstrumented adoption) is the correct structural defense against false-negative inference from missing telemetry (P33 structural-correctness alignment) and is reinforced by C3, DONT2, DONT3, and risk mitigations. The 'treat missing telemetry as unknown, not non-use' guardrail is stated in problem statement Boundaries, agreement Constraints (C3), design Key Decisions, and AC3 — consistent and non-contradictory across all four artifacts. Prep->packet trace accuracy is source-verified: the design's claim that prep does NOT consume docs/*-prep.md directly and that engineer packets split strict identity anchors from warn-first contextual anchors is backed by the actual renderer (advisory markers, no hard gate) and by the verification_missing consumer-warning path. Follow-ups are measurable: each of the 5 candidates carries an observable completion signal (zero-count query, per-change queryable count, non-null reuse count, pending/age distribution, end-to-end pack-citation test) and each is explicitly held out of this audit's scope (DONT + O4 + AC6 'no unapproved runtime change'). No blockers. Two minor notes: (1) the recorded clarify finding CLARIFY_UNCLEAR_SCOPE (no Scope section in proposal) is materially resolved downstream by the problem statement's explicit Scope block and the design's evidence model, so it is non-blocking. (2) AC1's fixed denominators (45 changes / 19 reflections) are point-in-time snapshot facts; measurement drift between design time and execution is a mild reproducibility risk already mitigated by the design's 'retain denominator/limitation in every conclusion' rule.

validation.notes: Contract coverage AC1-AC6/SC1-SC3/C1-C3/DONT1-3 fully mapped in design. Evidence-class model correctly prevents false inference from missing telemetry; guardrail stated consistently across problem statement, agreement, design. verification_missing correctly characterized (consumer-warning kind, not reflection friction category) — source-verified. Warn-first vs hard-gate packet enforcement claim source-verified against renderer. Follow-ups measurable and explicitly out of scope. Non-blocking: unresolved CLARIFY_UNCLEAR_SCOPE finding is materially satisfied by problem statement Scope block; AC1 fixed denominators carry mild snapshot-drift reproducibility risk already mitigated by the design's denominator-disclosure rule.

tradeoffs: Explicit evidence-class taxonomy (observed / contract-required / uninstrumented) adds analytical overhead per artifact but is the only structurally sound way to avoid absence-of-telemetry becoming a false negative.
Fixed baseline denominators (45 changes, 19 reflections) improve reproducibility and AC1 checkability but couple the acceptance target to a read-surface snapshot that may drift before execution.
Read-only boundary keeps the change safe and low-risk but defers all remediation value to separately-approved follow-ups, so this change ships insight, not fixes.

alternatives_considered.option: Infer artifact/pack adoption from presence or absence of counters
alternatives_considered.rationale: Design correctly rejects this via C3/DONT2/DONT3 and the evidence-class model; inferring non-use from absent telemetry would violate P33 structural-correctness and produce false negatives.

alternatives_considered.option: Propose workflow redesign from observed low retry counts
alternatives_considered.rationale: DONT1 and the design's key decision correctly scope observed gaps as instrumentation/bridge-enforcement gaps, not workflow-shape defects; low recorded retry is explicitly noted as omitting silent verification_missing warnings.

alternatives_considered.option: Bundle remediation (enforce durable verification evidence, persist research reports) into this change
alternatives_considered.rationale: Correctly deferred to measurable follow-up candidates with completion signals, preserving the read-only constraint (C1/O4/AC6).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to planning/design gate. The design is sound, contract coverage is complete, and evidence-integrity guardrails are structurally correct and source-verified. Recommend two small hardening moves that do not change scope: (1) in the execution report, capture the live denominators at run time alongside the design-time 45/19 baseline so AC1 remains checkable if the read surface drifted; (2) explicitly note in the report that the unresolved CLARIFY_UNCLEAR_SCOPE finding is satisfied by the problem-statement Scope block, closing the loop on that warning.

Artifact analysis distinguishes observed sample presence from uninstrumented adoption; it names most-used and least-durable artifacts without treating missing telemetry as non-use.

## Problem
Advance lacks a quantified, source-backed view of recurring agent failures, artifact use, workflow-friction hotspots, research-pack adoption, and whether prep and engineer packets carry sufficient implementation context.

## Scope
Survey durable ADV evidence from the last 10 days only. Include in-flight, archived, and closed changes created or active in that window, plus relevant agenda, wisdom, reflections, task state, and persisted sub-agent reports. Exclude speculative conclusions not supported by available evidence.

## Desired outcome
Produce a ranked audit that answers:
1. Most frequent agent issues.
2. Most-used and least-used artifacts/documents.
3. Workflow phases creating the most friction.
4. Whether research packs are used.
5. Whether prep aligns critical research/artifacts for implementers.
6. Whether adv-engineer packets provide adequate context.

## Boundaries
- Read-only analysis unless a separate follow-up is explicitly approved.
- Report counts, denominators, source types, confidence, and evidence gaps.
- Treat missing instrumentation as unknown, not negative evidence.

# Agreement — Audit agent workflow evidence

## Approved objective
Deliver a read-only, source-backed audit of Advance evidence from 2026-07-03 through 2026-07-13. Quantify recurring agent issues, artifact/document use, workflow friction, research-pack use, prep-to-implementation alignment, and adv-engineer context adequacy. Treat unavailable telemetry as unknown.

## Evidence baseline
- 45 retrievable changes; one terminal candidate omitted by the read surface.
- 19 reflection records.
- 286 agenda items.
- 13 change-scoped wisdom entries; 8 promoted project entries.
- Persisted sub-agent reports sampled across six representative changes.

## Findings to preserve
1. The strongest observed recurring issue is `verification_missing`: sampled engineer reports list verification commands without matching `adv_run_test` evidence.
2. Recorded retries are low (3 of 19 reflections), but this omits silent evidence-integrity warnings.
3. Largest recorded elapsed phases are planning (human approval) and acceptance (review/full-suite); execution is rarely the longest.
4. Proposal, agreement, design, and contract artifacts are consistently present in the sampled changes. Durable per-command verification evidence is weak; executive summaries are archive-weighted; problem statements are often folded into proposals.
5. Design-stage researcher/validator work is observed, but typed report persistence can degrade. Actual `docs/*-prep.md` adoption is not directly instrumented.
6. Prep maps approved artifacts into contract-linked tasks and briefing packets, but does not consume `docs/*-prep.md` directly. Engineer packets enforce identity anchors and contain contract/task/scope/affected-file/verification sections; scope/stop/verification anchors are warn-first and packet freshness is not a hard gate.

## Objectives
- O1: Report ranked issues with denominator, source, confidence, and limitation.
- O2: Separate lifecycle artifact presence from evidence durability and actual consumption.
- O3: Trace research-pack, prep, task, and briefing-packet behavior to source/spec evidence.
- O4: Recommend bounded, measurable follow-ups only; do not alter runtime behavior.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Audit covers 45 retrievable changes and 19 reflections in the requested window; reports the one omitted terminal candidate.
- AC2: Every ranked issue includes a count or bounded sample denominator, evidence source, and confidence level.
- AC3: Artifact analysis distinguishes observed sample presence from uninstrumented adoption; it names most-used and least-durable artifacts without treating missing telemetry as non-use.
- AC4: Research findings distinguish design-stage researcher/validator use from `docs/*-prep.md` pack consumption, and state persistence limitations.
- AC5: Prep-to-engineer analysis identifies artifact inputs, task/contract mapping, packet contents, and enforcement tier with source references.
- AC6: Report identifies at least three prioritized follow-ups, each with a measurable completion signal and no proposed unapproved runtime change.

## Success criteria
- SC1: Reader can answer all six original questions without relying on unverified claims.
- SC2: Report makes telemetry gaps explicit enough to turn into structural instrumentation work.
- SC3: No audit conclusion is based only on agent prose when an ADV state or source-contract citation exists.

## Constraints
- Read-only analysis; no code, spec, configuration, or runtime-state behavior changes.
- ADV MCP tools are authoritative for lifecycle state; repository source is authoritative for command/packet contracts.
- Do not infer non-use from absent counters or truncated agenda output.

## Avoidances
- No workflow redesign based solely on low retry counts.
- No claim that `docs/*-prep.md` packs are broadly adopted without direct measurement.
- No claim that adv-engineer context is sufficient without separating strict packet anchors, warn-first anchors, and unmeasured rendered-packet consumption.

## Extends
- Extends 19 persisted reflection records, 286 agenda records, wisdom records, and compact sub-agent reports from the requested window.
- No scoped `docs/*-prep.md` research pack was available as direct adoption evidence for this audit. New finding beyond prior records: prep has no direct research-pack consumer path, and packet enforcement is split between strict identity anchors and warn-first contextual anchors.

## Skills considered
- `adv-audit`: used for evidence-first, read-only audit discipline; partially applicable because this is workflow evidence rather than spec↔implementation drift.
- `adv-tron`: used for repository contract reconnaissance.
- `adv-researcher`: used for durable-state analysis.
- No additional skill required.

## LBP / external-solution check
No external alternatives apply. This is an internal evidence and workflow-contract audit; external research would not improve the stated conclusions.

## Conflict scan
- `adv_change_list includeArchived`: related work exists around agent routing, verifier, workflow directives, and archive behavior; none conflicts because this change is read-only.
- `adv_agenda_list`: substantial pending follow-up inventory confirms audit relevance; no mutation overlap.
- `adv_change_validate`: passed; `NO_TASKS` and `NO_DELTAS` are expected before planning for a non-code audit.

## Related-pattern scan
- Repeated source-vs-dist reload, targeted-test pollution, squash-merge proof, and branch-deploy hazards appear in wisdom/reflection evidence.
- Source reconnaissance found the same boundary pattern: artifacts are rendered/read at command time, while durable enforcement concentrates on typed identity/state boundaries.

## Edge cases / failure modes
- E1: Terminal candidate omitted from change listing. Mitigation: report the omission; do not claim a complete census.
- E2: Agenda response truncates item bodies. Mitigation: use total count and visible category evidence only; do not infer exact category-status distribution.
- E3: Research report persistence can degrade. Mitigation: distinguish work observed in gate evidence from durably queryable reports.
- E4: Briefing packets regenerate at read time. Mitigation: do not equate packet-schema availability with evidence that every engineer received the latest packet.

## Open design questions
None. This change delivers analysis only; any remediation requires a separate approved change.

## Draft spec deltas
No spec deltas required: scope is a read-only audit and makes no behavior change.

## AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS
- B1 boundary: resolved — last 10 days, durable ADV evidence and source contracts only.
- F1 functional: resolved — six named questions and AC1–AC6 define deliverable.
- S1 completion: resolved — measurable counts, citations, and follow-up criteria.
- M1 measurement: medium — some requested adoption metrics lack direct instrumentation; treated as explicit limitation, not inferred.
- Coverage: B PASS; F PASS; S PASS; M PASS with limitation.

documents.design:
# Design — Audit agent workflow evidence

## Delivery shape
A single read-only audit report, persisted through ADV change artifacts and supported by the typed researcher report. No repository files, behavior, specs, or runtime state change.

## Evidence model
| Question | Primary evidence | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|
| Recurring issues | persisted sub-agent reports, reflections, task recovery | state count/sample denominator; never prose-only conclusion |
| Artifact use | change artifacts/contracts plus command contracts | distinguish presence, consumption, and durability |
| Workflow friction | reflection per-gate elapsed and friction categories | do not equate low recorded retry with low true friction |
| Research packs | design-gate reports and source contracts for `docs/*-prep.md` | distinguish researcher use from pack use |
| Prep alignment | prep spec/readiness validator/task contract refs | separate prep input mapping from direct pack consumption |
| Engineer context | briefing-packet renderer, packet anchors, agent contract | classify strict, warn-first, and unmeasured fields |

## Source hierarchy
1. ADV MCP lifecycle state and typed reports — authoritative for recorded use/outcomes.
2. Repository source/spec/tests — authoritative for required and enforced behavior.
3. Reflections/wisdom/agenda — operational signal; bounded by their recording/truncation behavior.
4. Agent prose alone — supporting only; not sufficient where state/source evidence exists.

## Analysis procedure
1. Set the window and denominators: 45 retrievable changes, 19 reflections, 286 agenda records, 13 change-scoped wisdom records; disclose one omitted terminal candidate.
2. Group recorded friction by category and retain the distinction between counted friction and `verification_missing` warnings.
3. Classify artifacts as: observed presence, contract-required consumption, or uninstrumented adoption.
4. Trace the implementation-context path: approved artifacts → typed contract → prep task refs/evidence policy → rendered engineer briefing packet.
5. Audit the chain’s enforcement strength: runtime-enforced, test-enforced, or prose/spec-only.
6. Recommend bounded metrics/follow-ups, each with an observable completion signal.

## Key decisions
- **Use explicit evidence classes, not inferred adoption.** This prevents absence-of-telemetry from becoming a false negative.
- **Treat verification-missing as an evidence-integrity defect.** It is more frequent in the sampled reports than recorded retry failures, but it is not currently a reflection friction category.
- **Do not propose a workflow redesign.** Observed gaps are instrumentation and bridge-enforcement gaps.
- **Do not claim prep consumes research packs.** Source reconnaissance finds `docs/*-prep.md` consumption in discover, not prep.

## Follow-up candidates and signals
1. Enforce durable engineer verification evidence. Signal: `verification_missing` warning count reaches zero across a defined report sample and is emitted as reflection friction if nonzero.
2. Persist design research reports reliably. Signal: persisted-versus-degraded researcher/validator report count is queryable per change.
3. Instrument wisdom reuse. Signal: reflection output reports non-null reuse count and source references.
4. Add agenda-drain measurement. Signal: status exposes pending subagent-followup count and age distribution.
5. Bridge research-pack provenance into planning only if later product direction requires it. Signal: end-to-end test proves pack citation reaches task/briefing context; not in this audit’s scope.

## Risks and mitigations
- Terminal/listing omissions and truncated agenda output can bias counts. Mitigation: retain denominator/limitation in every conclusion.
- Rendered briefing-packet availability does not prove every worker received a current packet. Mitigation: label delivery adequacy as partially measured.
- Contract refs and warn-first anchors are not uniformly hard enforcement. Mitigation: classify enforcement tier rather than asserting completeness.

## Contract coverage
- AC1–AC4: procedure steps 1–3 and evidence model.
- AC5: procedure steps 4–5 and source hierarchy.
- AC6: follow-up candidates with completion signals.
- SC1–SC3 and C1–C3: source hierarchy, explicit classifications, and read-only boundary.
- DONT1–DONT3: key decisions and risks.

## No spec deltas
The audit changes no required behavior. Remediation remains separate, approved work.

# Executive Summary — Agent workflow evidence audit

## Outcome
Published a source-backed audit of Advance agent workflow evidence for the requested 10-day window: `docs/audits/agent-workflow-evidence-2026-07.md`.

## Value
The audit identifies evidence integrity—not task retry rate—as the highest-leverage workflow gap: sampled engineer reports repeatedly carry `verification_missing` warnings, while reflection metrics do not count those warnings as friction. It separates observed use from uninstrumented adoption, preventing false claims about research packs or briefing-packet delivery.

## Delivered
- Answers to all six requested questions with source, denominator, confidence, and limitations.
- Evidence hierarchy across ADV lifecycle state, typed reports, source contracts, reflections, wisdom, and agenda.
- Explicit artifact classifications: observed presence, contract-required consumption, uninstrumented adoption.
- Five measurable follow-up candidates: durable verification evidence, reliable design-research persistence, wisdom-reuse telemetry, agenda-drain telemetry, bounded archived-inclusive change listing.

## Verification
- Two planned tasks complete and checkpointed: `ccd8154b`, `31ca6419`.
- `adv_run_test tr_mrik4y4w_04333a8f` passed for document anchors.
- Independent verifier rubric review: PASS, high confidence; 15/15 contract rows pass or respected.
- Independent acceptance reviewer: READY; corrected research-pack citation scope before final checkpoint.

## Risks and follow-ups
- Snapshot values drifted during audit: 19→20 reflections and 286→291 agenda records. Report discloses both baseline and re-read values.
- Archived-inclusive change listing timed out during re-read; report retains the approved 45+1 baseline and treats re-verification as a known limitation.
- Research-pack consumption impact and actual briefing-packet delivery remain uninstrumented; neither is claimed as broad adoption.

## Release Readiness Summary
Harden review: READY. Worktree clean; only the approved audit document is committed. Acceptance matrix remains 15/15 pass/respected. Source-claim spot checks confirm bounded wording. No release blocker or ops/migration/frontend impact. Non-blocking release note: branch currently has no upstream; normal archive finalization must create/push its release handoff as needed.
